Prioritize Workers & Pages for all new applications. Use the official `wrangler` CLI for scaffolding and deployment. Always start with `wrangler generate`.
npx wrangler generate my-worker --type=module --ts
npx create-cloudflare@latest my-fullstack-app --framework next

Monorepos: use `pnpm` or `yarn workspaces`; centralize dependencies and build scripts (`"workspaces": ["apps/*", "packages/*"]`).

Manage secrets via `wrangler.toml` or the Cloudflare dashboard; use `.dev.vars` for local development. ❌ BAD: Storing sensitive data directly in code or `.env` files that aren't `.dev.vars`. Use `.dev.vars` for local secrets and integrate with CLI tools.
dotenv -e .dev.vars -- npx prisma migrate dev

Design for the edge: stateless Workers; use Durable Objects for stateful workloads. Workers are stateless and globally distributed. Avoid in-memory state that needs to persist across requests or instances. ❌ BAD: Relying on global variables for user sessions or shared data. Use KV for simple key-value storage, D1 for relational data, or Durable Objects for strong consistency and real-time state.

Use D1 for new, natively serverless relational databases; use Hyperdrive for edge acceleration to existing regional databases. Use R2 for large file storage (zero egress fees, global distribution).

Securely expose internal services without opening firewall ports; integrate SSO for private apps. Use `cloudflared` for secure access to Azure, AWS, GCP, or on-prem resources; present private web apps on Cloudflare-owned domains with SSO.
cloudflared tunnel create Azure-01

Keep Worker bundles small; tree-shake dependencies aggressively. ❌ BAD: Importing large, unoptimized libraries. Use `esbuild` and minimal imports. For Prisma, use `engineType: "client"` and an edge-compatible driver adapter to avoid large Rust binaries. ❌ BAD: Default Prisma setup with Rust query engines in Workers. Configure `schema.prisma`.

Leverage Cloudflare's CDN for static assets and API responses; set appropriate `Cache-Control` headers.

Workers runtime: single-threaded, event-driven, no Node.js APIs. Blocking I/O: Workers are single-threaded and event-driven. All I/O operations *must* be `await`ed. ❌ BAD: Synchronous file system operations or long-running CPU-bound tasks. Use asynchronous operations for network requests, KV, D1, etc.

Always configure WAF, Bot Fight Mode, and Rate Limiting. ❌ BAD: Deploying public APIs without edge security. Implement granular rate limiting for login endpoints, API abuse, and `cf_clearance` cookie reuse.

Test early, test often, and test at the edge. Use `Vitest` or `Jest` for unit tests; use `Miniflare` to locally emulate Workers runtime and KV, D1, R2 bindings. Use Playwright or Cypress for staging end-to-end tests.
npx wrangler deploy --env staging
npx playwright test --project=staging

Reference paths: `wrangler.toml`, `.dev.vars`, `src/index.ts`, `schema.prisma`, `my-logic.test.ts`, `./my-logic`, `worker.test.ts`, `dist/index.mjs`.
